schema_version.description: Format version of the report DOCUMENT envelope (meta/summary/groups/findings), independent of meta.version (the panopticon release) and meta.ocrdb_version. Optional for back-compat: legacy pre-5.1 reports omit it and read as version 0. #run7 DAT-F2A.

meta.description: #1602 ruling 4: CLOSED. `additionalProperties: false`, so a meta section the schema does not describe fails validation at RUN time, not only in tests/test_schema_parity.py -- which is how `host_capabilities` drifted for a whole release. Three producers write here and only three: `synth.report.assemble` (every section below except the four that follow), `synth.render.write_report` (`parts`, `discarded_claims_file`, `discarded_claims_count`) and `synth.report.attach_schema_status` (`schema_errors`). A new key means a schema entry in the same PR -- describe it, do not reopen this.

unverified_archive.description: #3332: present only on a report re-synthesized by `scripts/replay_report.py --trust-archive` from a run whose stamp (#3271) was NOT verified as this machine's -- a foreign archive. Its findings are the archive's own; nothing about where they came from was checked. Absent from every report a real run writes.

gate_security_mode.description: The security mode used by this report's gate, derived only from the controller-carried --security flag (standard when omitted). Unlike meta.security_mode, this never falls back to target-written groups.json. Absent on older reports.

parts.description: Basenames of the `<stem>_partN.json` continuation files this report was split into, written when the document exceeds the writer's byte budget. The main file then carries only the first chunk of `findings`, so a consumer that reads it alone has a PARTIAL report: hydrate the union before validating or comparing (synth/render._read_json_report is that reader).

discarded_claims_file.description: #15: basename of the `<stem>-discarded.json` sibling holding `discarded_claims` when the report is too large to carry them inline (rejected claims keep their full advisor prose and grow precisely when verification works well). Present only on a split report, and independent of `parts` -- the spill can happen with no findings chunking at all.

discarded_claims_count.description: #15: how many claims went to `discarded_claims_file`, so a reader of the main file alone still knows the size of what it is not holding.

schema_errors.description: #1639 P15: how many validation errors the PRE-WRITE pass (`synth.report.validate_report`: the published schema plus the domain rules the schema cannot express) raised against this report. Stamped after that pass, so it is in the artifact on disk but was not in the document that was validated. It is not the run's whole answer and must not be read as one: the artifact pass that follows re-validates the hydrated split union and the X0X sibling, which this count cannot include, and the `artifact invalid: N schema errors` status line carries that full count. Every artifact is still written either way -- a report that failed validation is on disk, with this count in it, precisely so it can be inspected.

tools.description: What the scanner layer meant for this run's REVIEWERS (#1637 P08) -- distinct from meta.coverage, which accounts for what the adapters produced.

panels_with_scanner_context.description: How many review panels were dispatched with tool output already on disk (`with`) and how many were not (`without`). Recorded per cell at the moment its prompt was rendered, so a run whose tool scan skipped cannot read like one that scanned. Both zero means no panel was dispatched at all.

disabled_mid_run.description: True when this run started with the tool scan enabled and had it switched off with --no-tools while in flight (#1637 P08) -- the non-destructive rescue from a scanner environment that moved after the scouts were paid for. Distinct from a run that never had tools at all, and stated on every report (false included) so its absence cannot be read as its not having been measured.

unplaceable.description: Per-tool counts of active findings with no placeable file under the target root.

network.description: What egress each scanner was given this run, per tool, copied off `tools-manifest.json` (#1645). `none` is the `--network none` containers -- every scanner but the two ONLINE_ONLY adapters. `proxied:<comma-separated hosts>` is an ONLINE_ONLY adapter that ran on a per-run `--internal` network behind a deny-by-default forward proxy allowing exactly those advisory endpoints; before this it got Docker's DEFAULT BRIDGE, i.e. every service reachable from the runner's network. `excluded:<reason>` is one whose egress could not be established: it did NOT run and did NOT fall back to the bridge, and it rides the manifest's `excluded_scope` rather than `selected`. `{}` on a run with no tools manifest, or one written without the scan loop ever running: nothing was measured, which is not the same claim as nothing was granted. The block is the runner's own, read as written (#3273): first contact and the manifest's run_id and output receipt vouch for the file, and the postures are the runner's own vocabulary.

sanitized.description: What an adapter refused to hand its scanner, per adapter, copied off `tools-manifest.json` (#1646). pip-audit is given a GENERATED requirements file holding only bare PEP 508 lines, because resolving an editable/local/VCS/URL requirement runs the reviewed repository's PEP 517 build backend -- so the dependency audit can be PARTIAL, and this says by how much and which lines. `{}` on a run with no tools manifest: nothing was measured, which is not the same claim as nothing was dropped. The block is the runner's own, read as written (#3273): first contact and the manifest's run_id and output receipt vouch for the file, and the producer caps it to 200 rows of at most 200 characters each.

source.description: The repo-relative manifest the lines came from (`requirements.txt`, `pyproject.toml`). Relative, never absolute: the report is published and an absolute path would carry the scanner host's layout into it. A candidate manifest that resolved OUTSIDE the target -- a symlinked `requirements.txt` -- is treated as absent and named here as `<name> outside target`, so a repo whose manifest escapes the tree cannot read like a repo that has none.

kept.description: How many lines were audited -- the size of the generated file the scanner was actually given.

dropped.description: One row per line that was NOT audited. URL credentials are masked at the producer (scripts.tools.pip_audit), because these lines are target-authored text.

line.description: The line as evaluated: `\` continuations joined, comments and `--hash=` tokens removed, credentials masked.

reason.description: Why it could not be audited. One of: `editable`; `local path`; `archive name` (a bare name pip resolves as a local archive on a suffix match -- `evil.tar.gz` -- before it considers whether the string looks like a path at all); `vcs url`; `direct url`; `option line`; `include` (a `-r`/`-c` the pure grammar classified but did not resolve -- the pyproject branch never resolves includes, so this reaches the manifest there); `include outside target`; `nested include`; `include unreadable`; `unparseable`.

hashes_stripped.description: True when at least one `--hash=` token was removed from a kept line. pip-audit does not need them, and one left in would impose `--require-hashes` semantics the generated file cannot satisfy.

truncated.description: True when the source manifest was larger than the adapter would read (1 MiB or 20,000 lines, whichever bit first), so lines beyond the bound were neither audited nor disclosed. The read is capped because this text is target-authored and lands in two published artifacts; the cap is stated rather than applied silently, which would be a second partial audit nobody was told about.

dropped_truncated.description: How many further dropped lines exist beyond the 200 listed in `dropped`. 0 when the list is complete. The rows are capped for the same reason the read is; the COUNT is always exact.

image.description: The tools image this run's scan was DISPATCHED BY, copied off `tools-manifest.json` (#3270). The audit's provenance rule is that the tools image digest is the unit of trust, so run_tools resolves its tag to the image ID (`docker image inspect`'s `.Id`, the content digest of the image config) and runs the containers by that id; a tag moved mid-run cannot swap the image. `repo_digests` are informational: a local `docker build` image has none. `adapter_code` is one sha256 over the controller checkout's `skill/scripts`, which every dispatch mounts over the image's baked copy -- the code the id does not cover. `id` null means the image was not available and the tool scan was skipped. Absent when no runner recorded an image. Repaired at the read (`scripts.tools_image.repair`): the manifest is target-writable, so a value out of shape is dropped to null.

prior_run.description: This run started over an earlier run by ANOTHER host in the same `.panopticon/` (#3271, ruling D2). The earlier run carries this machine's run stamp, so it is ours and is disclosed rather than halted on. Absent otherwise.

run_id.description: The first 8 hex characters of the earlier run's run_id.

apps.description: Every external app this run launched, named rather than trusted (#3270): the host CLI the posture was probed through (off host-capabilities.json) and docker (off tools-manifest.json). One shape per app; a field the machine could not answer is null and `reason` says which step failed. #3272 keys its probe cache on `sha256` and `version` together. Absent when none was recorded. Repaired at both reads (`scripts.app_trace.repair`).

path.description: The resolved executable's realpath, with the operator's home spelled `~` in the report (#3271); the manifests keep the full path.

version.description: The first line `<app> --version` printed, at most 200 printable characters.

coverage.description: What this run actually did: which adapters produced usable output, which tools ran, verify-phase accounting, and the tool-policy posture.

adapters.description: Per output file: {status: ok|empty|noscan|failed, findings: int, reason?: str, file_coverage?: object}. file_coverage separates usable scanner output from complete file coverage: status complete|partial, parsed_files/unparsed_files/unavailable_files counts, bounded files [{file, reason}], files_omitted, and capabilities_unavailable. Partial captures keep their genuine findings and baseline eligibility; summary.coverage_certified is false with an explicit coverage_note. A failed file (0-byte, unparseable, or no registered adapter) is not counted as having run. noscan (#1335) = the adapter ran and produced a valid document but scanned zero files, so it gets no coverage credit. suppressed_in_source?: int (#1839) = how many of that tool's results this run honoured an INLINE suppression comment over (semgrep's `# nosemgrep`), dropped at the parse under `--security standard` and kept under redteam; an absent key means none were, which is not the same claim as 0.

tools_file_partial.description: Adapters with usable captures but incomplete file coverage, mapped to the same bounded file_coverage facts in adapters. Reasons: parse_error or typescript_parser_unavailable; for semgrep (#2957) rule_timeout (a rule ran past the stated per-file timeout, so its findings there are missing) or timeout_abandoned (the stated threshold of rules timed out, so no rule's findings from that file survive), each with rule_timeouts, plus a run total rule_timeouts and unlocated_records for timeouts whose file could not be identified; or (#3193) size_skipped (over the stated size_limit, so Semgrep never read it), listed by the host at capture, with the run total size_skipped and size_listing (listed, or absent / malformed / incomplete, each one more unlocated record: a capture without a complete listing is never read as nothing skipped). Findings still gate; file gaps alone do not invalidate a baseline or change the finding-based gate. summary.coverage_certified is false.

tools_ran.description: Adapters whose run earns coverage credit (status ok or empty). Excludes noscan: an adapter that scanned zero files covered nothing (#1335).

build_executing_tools.description: Names of adapters from EXECUTES_TARGET_BUILD that ran this run (produced an output file), whether or not they emitted findings.

target_build_not_run.description: #3265 (owner ruling 2026-10-23): adapters from EXECUTES_TARGET_BUILD that applied to the target but were NOT run, because the operator did not pass --allow-target-build. Running one executes the target's own build code inside the tools container, so it is opt-in and off by default. Present only when something was withheld. Read off the tools manifest's `withheld` list and repaired to EXECUTES_TARGET_BUILD names (the manifest is target-writable). Non-sinking: an off-by-default adapter is never `missing` and never affects coverage_certified.

dependency_audit.description: #3269 SCA: the runner's repaired dependency-coverage receipt. applicable names deterministic dependency ecosystems in the tree; selected and produced name only dedicated SCA adapters intersected with the runner's actual selection and output receipt, and produced is further reconciled against usable ingest coverage. Failed or forged output and empty Trivy SARIF earn no credit. A non-empty applicable list with no produced adapter makes coverage NOT CERTIFIED and a PASS gate INCONCLUSIVE. `unknown` is the fixed fail-closed repair of a malformed target-adjacent receipt. The key is absent on legacy/direct manifests that never measured this axis.

tool_policy_mode.description: Posture of the fan-out reviewer entries (panel_review/lens_sweep) derived from dispatch plans; scout/advisor posture is not recorded. "unknown" means no dispatch plan was found.

verdicts.description: Verify-phase accounting: verdicts that were dropped are otherwise stderr-only, and under strict gating a run whose verdicts all failed to match looks like a clean pass.

unanswered.description: Queued findings left without a verdict; null when no --verdicts-dir was supplied, i.e. not measured.

misrouted.description: #1475: verdict files that EXISTED for the cell they were written for but could not be bound to it -- the finding_id echo named a different finding, or none. Also counted in `unanswered` (the finding has no valid verdict either way), but the cause is the OPPOSITE of a missing dispatch: an advisor ran, adjudicated, and mislabelled its answer. Reported separately so the two are distinguishable without reading agent transcripts.

unloadable.description: Verdict files or entries present on disk but un-loadable: a file that is corrupt or invalid JSON, or (#2990) an entry of a loadable verdict bundle that is not an object, names no known verdict, or echoes no finding_id. Their findings are left unverified. A non-zero count means verification evidence was lost, distinct from a verdict that was never generated (#938).

fan_out.description: Planned-vs-executed fan-out coverage derived at synthesis from the dispatch plan and the findings files on disk: {planned, executed, groups_complete, groups_partial}. null when no dispatch plan was present.

scout_profiles_seen.description: Scout profiles harvested; with scout_requested, distinguishes 'no scouts ran' (0) from 'scouts ran and requested no tools' (N>0 with []).

scout_requested.description: Union of tools requested across scout profiles.

out_of_scope.description: #441 reviewer scope disclosure: {checked, count, examples} of findings citing files outside their group's assigned list; null when no plan/group could be checked.

doc_policy.description: #487 planning-doc severity policy disclosure: {downgraded, examples}; null when redteam bypassed the policy.

divergence.description: Planned-vs-executed gaps: {panels: {name: {planned, executed}}, tools: {name: 'requested_absent'|'produced_unusable'|'requested_unavailable'|'produced_noscan'|'network_unavailable'}}. network_unavailable (safe egress could not be established), requested_absent (selected, no output) and produced_unusable (#1512: output produced but ingestion could not parse it) are lost required coverage and reach tools_absent, so they gate. requested_unavailable (scout asked for a tool the runner cannot run) and produced_noscan (#1335: ran but scanned zero files) are disclosure only and never gate.

cells.description: 5.0 (matrix Sec5.1) certifiable-coverage audit of the FLOOR cells: `{"missing_floor": [[group, domain], ...]}`. A floor (group, domain) cell that produced no findings file is lost required coverage, and a non-empty list is what forces the gate to INCONCLUSIVE. Scout-WIDENED domains are never audited here -- the floor is the contract -- and a floor domain the group explicitly excluded is netted out first.

reviewed.description: Optional measured completed review cells as sorted [group, DOMAIN] pairs, preserving exact group/chunk identity. Derived from ingested agent findings paths after malformed cells are removed; empty means measured with none completed, omission means unknown. Tool findings never establish agent-cell review. Disclosure only; missing_floor remains the coverage gate.

planned_pairs.description: Optional measured planned review cells as sorted [group, DOMAIN] pairs from coverage records' effective domains, preserving exact group/chunk identity. Published with reviewed when ingested-path and plan measurement exist; omission means unknown. An empty panel cell has zero findings with complete review only when every nonempty planned domain for that group/panel is reviewed. Disclosure only; coverage gates are unchanged.

tools_suppressed.description: #1578/#1740/#1839/#3269 G4: `{reason: count}` for findings withheld from `findings[]` by Panopticon's controlled source-scope rules. `run-artifact` counts findings under a top-level `.panopticon`, `.worktrees` or `.git`; `generated-bytecode` counts findings under `__pycache__` or ending in `.pyc`/`.pyo`. Existing keys name vendored and virtualenv path segments, the reserved `fixture-corpus` rule, marker-confirmed virtualenv paths (`pyvenv.cfg:<dir>`), or scan-side virtualenv classes. Keys equal to `virtualenv-by-marker` or `virtualenv-by-name` count directories the scanner skipped; every other key counts findings dropped at ingest. The findings remain absent from the report body. `run-artifact` and `generated-bytecode` are disclosed in both modes and gated in neither; under redteam they remain here and are also named by `tools_suppressed_not_gated`. For other reasons, redteam can move CRITICAL and secret-class findings into `tools_suppressed_gated`; declined or otherwise scoped-out findings stay here, with the policy-C subset also named by `tools_suppressed_not_gated`. Operator-authored exclusion globs are policy, not suppression, and appear only in `tools_excluded`. `{}` is an explicit measured zero. The read boundary repairs counts and bounds the map to 200 keys; overlong target-derived names are marked and cut, with colliding counts summed.

tools_suppressed_gated.description: #1701/#3269 G4: `{reason: count}` for source-scope-suppressed findings that remain absent from `findings[]` but THIS RUN'S redteam gate counted. Policy C admits only CRITICAL or secret-class findings; the driver then applies its operator-selected severity and delta/gate-scope filters. This map never includes `run-artifact` or `generated-bytecode`, which are gated in neither mode. Read beside `tools_suppressed`: per reason, the two counts partition what ingest suppressed from the body into gated and not gated. `{}` is the standard-mode answer and any redteam run where no suppressed finding moved the gate. These findings bypass tool verification because they are not in the report body.
tools_suppressed_gated.$comment: Repaired to these types at the read by synth.repair.repair_tools_suppressed, like its sibling.

tools_suppressed_not_gated.description: #1578 policy C, widened through #3269 G4: `{reason: count}` for source-scope-suppressed findings that cleared the run's severity and delta/gate-scope filters but the redteam gate declined. It includes rows policy C declined because they were neither CRITICAL nor secret-class, plus every `run-artifact` or `generated-bytecode` candidate regardless of severity or secret provenance. This is a subset of `tools_suppressed`, not a third population beside it, and is empty in standard mode.
tools_suppressed_not_gated.$comment: Repaired to these types at the read by synth.repair.repair_tools_suppressed, like its two siblings.

language_detection_skips.description: #3247: language-keyed scanners auto-detection did not select because their language appeared only below #1138's reviewable-but-selection-pruned directory names. Each row is a controlled language/tool pair and one fixed reason; synthesis repairs the target-writable tools manifest to this enum and cap without re-deriving selection. `[]` means automatic detection measured no such gap. The key is absent when explicit `--languages` or `--tools` bypassed automatic detection. Disclosure only: it changes neither tool selection nor certification.

globs.description: The path globs that scoped this run's tool ingest: the repository's committed top-level `exclude_paths:` (threaded by the driver as `--tools-exclude`, and to the scan as `run_tools --exclude`), or whatever an operator passed directly. Published even when a glob matched nothing this run -- the policy scoped the run either way, and a reader comparing two runs has to see it. Repaired at the read (`synth.repair.repair_tools_excluded`): a non-string or over-long glob is dropped rather than cut, because a cut glob is a different glob and would misstate the policy.

count.description: How many TOOL findings the operator's path globs dropped at ingest. Distinct from `tools_suppressed`/`tools_suppressed_gated`: suppression is a controlled Panopticon source-scope rule whose eligible CRITICAL or secret-class findings can still gate under `--security redteam`, except that `run-artifact` and `generated-bytecode` are disclosure-only. An exclusion is operator or repository policy and is counted, disclosed, and never re-admitted in any mode.

tools_excluded.description: #1740 (ARC-F2A, fix round 2): the exclusion POLICY this run's tool ingest applied, and what it removed. `exclude_paths:` is authored by the repository under review and (since #1740) scopes the scanners, this report and the gate, so a committed `['**']` that empties the tool axis is a fact the ARTIFACT must carry -- it was visible only in `groups.json`, `tools-manifest.json` and an ingest stderr line nobody keeps. Stated on every report, `{"globs": [], "count": 0}` included: the field's absence must never be readable as `nothing was excluded`. `security_gate.py` prints the same two numbers beside its own verdict line. What this count does NOT measure is the larger half of the same decision: on a driver run these globs ARE the committed `exclude_paths:`, and `discovery` prunes the matching files before any grouping (#1136, the `exclude_paths` prune in `discovery.py` -- they land in neither a group nor a leftover), so no REVIEW CELL of any domain saw them either, SEC included, which a per-group `exclude:` could never do (#1084). Since #1757 (owner ruling 2026-09-25) that is true of every domain BUT SEC; since #3338 every code-shaped file is on that SEC floor. `discovery` keeps those files in a dedicated SEC-only review group and publishes them under `exclude_paths_sec_carve_out` beside this block. Explicit documentation and known assets remain prunable. The run-14 findings SEC-1915770944 / AGT-1355709320 are what the original ruling answered, and this description used to call the whole-domain prune the feature rather than a gap; the summary line says the narrowed version in one clause. A direct `synthesize --tools-exclude` is the exception: those globs scoped this ingest alone.

kind.description: Stable cleanup-failure class recorded by the scanner capture path, such as cidfile_unreadable, cidfile_empty, kill_launch_failed, or kill_failed.

detail.description: Redacted, single-line operator detail for the cleanup failure. The capture path bounds it before stderr and manifest output; synthesis repairs and bounds the target-writable manifest again.

tools_cleanup_failures.description: Scanner containers whose best-effort timeout cleanup could not prove them stopped, keyed by scanner. This is an operator-visible resource and coverage condition carried from the same capture event as the stderr diagnostic. It does not replace the scanner's ordinary timeout or missing-output result and does not change that result's existing gate behavior. The block is omitted when no cleanup failure occurred and read as written (#3273): the capture path bounds and redacts each detail when it records it.

globs.description: The committed top-level `exclude_paths:` globs that scoped this exclusion -- the same list `tools_excluded.globs` carries on a driver run. Published even when they carved nothing, because the policy scoped the run either way.

files.description: The repo-relative paths those globs matched AND the deterministic code-group SEC floor also matched (`coverage_model.applicable_sec_floor`, asked one file at a time) -- the code-shaped files that reach the SEC domain anyway, in the dedicated `exclude_paths_sec_carve_out` review group. Repaired at the read (`synth.repair.repair_sec_carve_out`): a non-string or over-long path is DROPPED rather than cut, because a cut path names a file that does not exist, and the list is bounded -- so a list shorter than `count` is the honest reading of both.

count.description: How many files the carve-out kept for SEC review. The MEASUREMENT, not a recount of the list above: it survives the bound applied to `files`.

exclude_paths_sec_carve_out.description: #1757 (AGT-1355709320), owner ruling 2026-09-25: *a target-authored `exclude_paths` may not remove a file the deterministic SEC floor matches from the SEC domain; such an exclusion is disclosed in the report's coverage section instead of silently applied. Other domains keep honouring the exclusion.* Since #3338 that floor includes every code-shaped file, while explicit documentation and known assets remain prunable. This key is that disclosure. The floor exists so operator taste cannot hide code from security review, and SEC is already NON_EXCLUDABLE against a per-group `exclude:` (#1084) -- but the top-level path prune ran BEFORE grouping and reached the same outcome through an unguarded door, which is the asymmetry run-14 found. A review cell is (group x domain) and no domain can be restricted to a subset of a group's files, so `discovery` puts the carved files in one dedicated group named `exclude_paths_sec_carve_out` whose coverage is pinned to exactly `["SEC"]` (`phases/coverage.py`, off the group entry's `sec_carve_out` marker); they do NOT rejoin their natural groups, so COD/ARC/TST and the rest still honour the exclusion. The TOOL axis is unchanged -- see `tools_excluded`. ABSENT, not zero, on a run that committed no `exclude_paths:` at all: zero behaviour change is zero output change, the rule `groups.json`'s own `exclude_paths` key already follows. Present with `count: 0` when globs were committed and matched no code-shaped file. An operator-authored `--pr` config gets the same treatment, deliberately: the ruling's rationale is that nobody's taste hides code from security review. SCOPE: like every other per-run disclosure this describes THIS RUN's surface, so a narrowing scope flag narrows it -- `--scope-dir` keeps the carved files under that directory, while `--scope-file` and `--scope-group` carve nothing at all (their universes come out of the already-pruned listing). A `count: 0` on a scoped run therefore means "nothing in this run's scope", not "nothing in the repository" -- unlike `groups.json`'s `excluded_count`, which those three flags leave at the whole-repo number.

test_inventory.description: #1638 P13: per REVIEW UNIT -- the root config's `groups:` entry, so a run-time `<name>_N` chunk answers as its parent -- whether the test inventory that unit's reviewers were shown could be believed: complete (it holds tests, or holds no code at all), empty (it holds code and no test, on either the `tests:` axis or in its own file list), or split (test files named after its modules are claimed by another unit). Recorded by the review phase as each prompt was rendered. An empty or split entry means a `TST` no-coverage claim from that unit may be a defect in the MATRIX, not in the target's test suite; run-13 published exactly that claim for a module whose 138 tests the same session had run green. No agent files a finding for it -- the state is driver-computed and published here. `{}` means this run did not measure it (a direct synthesize.py call), which is a different fact from every unit being complete.

repo.description: Which repository carried the setting: `.` for the review root, else the submodule's path relative to it.

key.description: The config key that was emptied, e.g. `filter.lfs.clean`. The VALUE is never published: it is a command line the reviewed tree authored.

git_drivers_suppressed.description: #2013: the TARGET's own Git driver commands this scan ran with EMPTIED. Every git call on a review target goes through a probe that refuses to run a command the reviewed tree configured (#1985/#2006); refusing such a target outright made a git-lfs (`git lfs install --local`) or git-crypt checkout unreviewable on every path that touches git, so the probe now overrides each `filter.*.clean/.process/.smudge`, `diff.external` and `diff.*.command/.textconv` it finds with `-c <key>=` (plus that driver's `required` flag, which would otherwise turn the emptied command into a hard error), proves each override took, and discloses the keys here. It changes what git COMPARES, not what any reviewer was shown (agents read the worktree; the probe never checks anything out): a clean filter is what makes the index blob equal the worktree, so paths under a suppressed driver compare as MODIFIED — dirtiness for them is unknown and a delta may include them. That is why this rides the artifact and not only the run manifest, and why a delta-scoped run over such a comparison cannot certify its coverage (see meta.integrity.delta_scope_suppressed_git_drivers). Stated on every report, `[]` included: the field's absence must never be readable as `the target configured none`. `[]` means no driver was emptied under this run's probe; it does NOT distinguish a run whose manifest predates this field, which the driver also threads as nothing (reachable only on a run resumed across that upgrade). Repaired at the read (`synth.repair.repair_git_drivers_suppressed`): the key half is repository-authored.

resume.description: Resume accounting for fan-out/verify phases; null on fresh full runs.

delta.description: Delta-review disclosure (#449); null outside delta mode, which includes a payload that was rejected or carried no `base` -- a run that was GIVEN a diff-hunks path says so in the sibling `delta_artifact` below, which is how a rejected artifact is told apart from a run that was never passed `--diff-hunks` (#2169). Every key is pinned under `properties` so the schema-parity walk descends into this block (#2169, #1602 in miniature); the seven keys copied verbatim out of `.panopticon/diff-hunks.json` are type-pinned too, and safely so, because the loader now REPAIRS them at the read (#2382): a value of the wrong type is read as null and named in `delta_artifact.keys_repaired`, so the pin states what the read already enforces instead of letting a hand-supplied artifact end a paid-for run on a terminal schema error. The driver's discovery phase rewrites or removes that file, so the exposure the repair closes is the direct `synthesize.py --diff-hunks <path>` invocation, not a `driver run`.

base.description: The base the artifact resolved, copied verbatim from it (normally a ref or commit string); any truthy value is what makes the review a delta one. Never null here: a `base` the artifact omitted or that was repaired at the read (see `delta_artifact.keys_repaired`) makes the review a non-delta one, and this whole block is null instead.

base_source.description: How the artifact says it chose that base (`explicit`, `fallback`, ...), copied verbatim from it. Null when absent from the artifact or repaired at the read (see `delta_artifact.keys_repaired`).

base_commit.description: The artifact's own anchor commit for the base, so a later reader can reconstruct the delta after branch tips move; null when it resolved none. Null when absent from the artifact or repaired at the read (see `delta_artifact.keys_repaired`).

delta_start.description: The artifact's own anchor commit for the start of the delta; null when it resolved none. Null when absent from the artifact or repaired at the read (see `delta_artifact.keys_repaired`).

delta_end.description: The artifact's own anchor commit for the end of the delta; null when it resolved none. Null when absent from the artifact or repaired at the read (see `delta_artifact.keys_repaired`).

includes_uncommitted.description: Whether the artifact says the diff it measured included uncommitted worktree changes. Null when absent from the artifact or repaired at the read (see `delta_artifact.keys_repaired`).

files_changed.description: The ARTIFACT's own count of changed files, which is not the size of the map this run classified against -- compare `hunks_files` below. Null when absent from the artifact or repaired at the read (see `delta_artifact.keys_repaired`).

diff_context.description: Lines of tolerance this run allowed around a hunk when classifying a finding on-diff (`--diff-context`, default 5).

hunks_files.description: Files in the hunk map this run actually classified against; 0 on an ACTIVE delta means the map matched no finding, so every one classified off-diff and a `--gate-scope on-diff` gate had nothing left to fail on.

hunks_ranges.description: Line ranges in that same map. 0 on an ACTIVE delta with gate-eligible findings present under `--gate-scope on-diff` makes that run read INCONCLUSIVE rather than PASS (#2178, narrowed by #2222); with no such finding it keeps its PASS, because a legitimately empty change is not a defect. A named file with no range of its own is a separate hazard: a finding there fails OPEN to on-diff.

ranges_dropped.description: Malformed hunk ranges the loader discarded -- one per range that was not a two-integer pair. The file stays in the map and is merely narrower; a WHOLE lost path is counted separately as `paths_dropped` (#2169), not as one of these. Since #2405, widened by #2517 (owner ruling 2026-10-02), a non-zero value here is one of the FOUR shapes -- with `paths_dropped`, `paths_emptied_by_drops` and `payload_malformed` -- that turn a PASS gate INCONCLUSIVE under `--gate-scope on-diff` when gate-eligible findings exist: the map that chose the gate's scope is provably damaged. Null when this context was not built by reading a file.

paths_dropped.description: Whole paths the loader discarded, because the value under the path was not a list of ranges at all (#2169). Such a file leaves the map entirely, so every finding in it classifies off-diff -- a strictly more expensive loss than a dropped range. Since #2517 (owner ruling 2026-10-02) a non-zero value here is one of the FOUR shapes -- with `ranges_dropped`, `paths_emptied_by_drops` and `payload_malformed` -- that turn a PASS gate INCONCLUSIVE under `--gate-scope on-diff` when gate-eligible findings exist (the reason lands in `summary.coverage_note`). Its direction is the fail-OPEN one: the dropped file's findings LEFT the gate's source set rather than being admitted to it, so such a run reported a PASS over findings the artifact had hidden. It never fires on a legitimate change shape, because the loader drops a path only for a value that is not a list at all and no `diff_map.parse` output produces one. Null when this context was not built by reading a file.

paths_without_ranges.description: Paths the map NAMES whose list of ranges is empty (#2381). Not a loss: the file stays in the map, and every finding in it classifies ON-diff by `diff_map.classify`'s changed-file fail-open, so under `--gate-scope on-diff` every finding in this many files is admitted to the gate's source set on the artifact's word rather than on a measured range. Non-zero is not by itself a defect -- a deletion-only, binary, mode-only or same-content rename change legitimately carries a key with no range -- but a truncated or hand-edited map looks exactly the same from here, and no other key in either block distinguishes them: `ranges_dropped` and `paths_dropped` are both zero for this shape, and the whole-map disclosures require `hunks_ranges: 0`. Classification is unchanged by this counter; the gate reads only its `paths_emptied_by_drops` subset (#2405); the remainder is disclosed, never reclassified. A path whose every range was malformed is counted BOTH here and in `ranges_dropped` -- two facts about one path, and `paths_emptied_by_drops` below is how many of the paths counted here are of that kind. Null when this context was not built by reading a file.

paths_emptied_by_drops.description: How many of `paths_without_ranges` above arrived NON-empty and were emptied by the loader because every range under the path was malformed (#2386): the sub-population a BROKEN artifact produced, as opposed to the one that arrived `[]`. That difference (`paths_without_ranges` minus this) is what it recovers -- a gate rule can treat this count as suspicious without firing on every legitimate deletion-only, binary, mode-only or same-content rename change, which the merged counter could not. Since #2405 a non-zero value here, a non-zero `ranges_dropped`, a non-zero `paths_dropped` (#2517, the fourth shape), or a set `payload_malformed` turns a PASS gate INCONCLUSIVE under `--gate-scope on-diff` when gate-eligible findings exist (the reason lands in `summary.coverage_note`); it never fires on a legitimate deletion-only change and knowingly misses a truncated map that arrived `[]`. A subset, not a sibling: every path counted here is also counted in `paths_without_ranges`, and every one of them dropped at least one range, so `ranges_dropped` is non-zero too. Classification is unchanged by either counter. Null when this context was not built by reading a file.

payload_malformed.description: Why the payload was rejected in whole or in part, from the closed vocabulary `unreadable` / `not an object` / `hunks not an object` / `unsupported schema_version` / `generation-mismatch`. Only `hunks not an object` can reach this block, because the other four -- `unsupported schema_version` included, which rejects the whole payload (#2382), and `generation-mismatch`, which rejects an artifact whose `run_id` is not the one the reader was told to expect (#2107): a hunk map from a different discovery generation than this run's `groups.json`, so the review covered one surface and the gate would have scoped to another -- leave no `base` and hence no delta review; there the sibling `delta_artifact` carries the reason. The #2405 gate rule NAMES this key so its measure is total over that vocabulary, but no value here can publish its reason: `hunks not an object` leaves the hunk map empty, so `hunks_ranges` is 0 and such a run reads INCONCLUSIVE under the older zero-hunk refusal (#2178) instead. Null when nothing was rejected, and null when this context was not built by reading a file.

on_diff_total.description: Active findings this run classified as on-diff.

pre_existing_total.description: Active findings this run classified as pre-existing (off-diff).

delta_artifact.description: What ATTEMPTING to read `.panopticon/diff-hunks.json` cost: an object whenever a `--diff-hunks` path was given and a read was attempted -- whether or not it succeeded, and whether or not the resulting delta was active -- and null when none was given (a direct caller, or a run never passed the flag), so the block's presence alone is the fact (#2169). That is what it publishes: a rejected payload carries no `base`, so `delta` above is null exactly as it is for a run given no artifact at all, and rather than dressing a rejection up as an active delta, `delta` is left alone for consumers that read its truthiness as "this was a delta review".

payload_malformed.description: Why the payload was rejected in whole or in part, from the same closed vocabulary `delta.payload_malformed` uses; unlike that key, all five values can appear here, including the four (`unreadable` -- which covers a path that does not exist -- `not an object`, `unsupported schema_version`, which rejects a payload carrying a `schema_version` that is not the int 1, and `generation-mismatch`, which rejects a payload whose `run_id` is not the generation the reader was told to expect: the driver's discovery phase stamps both halves of a delta discovery and the synthesize phase passes `--diff-hunks-run-id`, so a hunk map from another generation than this run's `groups.json` -- or one carrying no stamp at all -- is refused rather than scoping this run's gate. A hand-run `synthesize.py` is covered too: with no flag the expectation defaults to the `run_id` on the `groups.json` that run read, and only an inventory carrying no stamp either leaves the payload unchecked. The refusal is published HERE rather than being withheld at the phase, so it is told apart from a run that was never a delta one, #2107) that leave no `base` and so no `delta` block at all. The #2405 gate rule names this key so its measure is total over the vocabulary, and no value here reaches that reason in a real run: `hunks not an object` is the only one that leaves an ACTIVE delta and it empties the hunk map, so the zero-hunk refusal (#2178) is what such a run publishes, while the other four degrade the gate to the wider scope, which fails closed. Null when nothing was rejected.

keys_repaired.description: The artifact-carried keys of `meta.coverage.delta` that carried a value of the wrong type and were read as NULL (#2382), in the loader's table order: `base`, `base_source`, `base_commit`, `delta_start`, `delta_end`, `includes_uncommitted`, `files_changed`. Empty when every one of those the artifact carried had the type pinned for it above; a key ABSENT from the artifact is not a repair, because `meta.coverage.delta` publishes it as null either way. `base` in this list is the expensive entry: the review is NOT a delta one, `delta` above is null exactly as it is for a run given no artifact, and the gate scopes to every active finding -- which is why the list lives in THIS block, the one written whenever `--diff-hunks` was passed, rather than in the block the repair can null. A repair is also printed on stderr in the #957 register. Never null here, because this block is written only when a read was attempted.

ranges_dropped.description: Malformed hunk ranges the loader discarded, as `delta.ranges_dropped` -- one of the four shapes that turn an on-diff PASS gate INCONCLUSIVE (#2405, the fourth added by #2517); never null here, because this block is written only when a read was attempted.

paths_dropped.description: Whole paths the loader discarded, as `delta.paths_dropped` -- since #2517 (owner ruling 2026-10-02) one of the four shapes that turn an on-diff PASS gate INCONCLUSIVE when gate-eligible findings exist, and the fail-OPEN one: the dropped file leaves the map, so every finding in it classifies off-diff and leaves the gate's source set instead of being admitted to it. Never null here, for the same reason as its siblings.

paths_without_ranges.description: Paths the map names with no range of their own, as `delta.paths_without_ranges` -- the fail-open shape, in which every finding in such a file reaches a `--gate-scope on-diff` gate as on-diff; never null here, for the same reason as its siblings. `paths_emptied_by_drops` below splits them, and the gate reads only that subset (#2405); the remainder is disclosed, never reclassified.

paths_emptied_by_drops.description: How many of `paths_without_ranges` above the loader emptied itself, because every range under the path was malformed, as `delta.paths_emptied_by_drops` -- the sub-population a BROKEN artifact produced, told apart from the one that arrived `[]` (#2386). It recovers which rangeless paths came from a damaged artifact. Since #2405 a non-zero value here, a non-zero `ranges_dropped`, a non-zero `paths_dropped` (#2517, the fourth shape), or a set `payload_malformed` turns a PASS gate INCONCLUSIVE under `--gate-scope on-diff` when gate-eligible findings exist (the reason lands in `summary.coverage_note`); it never fires on a legitimate deletion-only change and knowingly misses a truncated map that arrived `[]`. That rule needs an ACTIVE delta, i.e. a read that resolved a `base` and so published the `delta` block above; a payload rejected outright leaves no `base`, and there the gate degrades to the wider scope, which fails closed. Never null here, for the same reason as its siblings.

clamped.description: Reasoned overrides whose requested severity synthesis reduced to the OCRDb range/rung limit.

missing.description: Agent findings reverted to the OCRDb default because an off-default severity omitted severity_override. Tool severities are excluded.

verify_matrix.description: P5 verify-matrix accounting: engaged (>= F_p) cell count and the engaged cells left unverified (which force gate INCONCLUSIVE).

host_capabilities.description: 5.2 surface 2 (#1344 F3b): the host posture this run VERIFIED, copied verbatim off `runs/<tag>/host-capabilities.json`. Documented in prose since #1344 and undescribed here until #1602 -- the drift the parity test (tests/test_schema_parity.py) now exists to prevent. Every field fails closed (`null`, `{}` for the maps) on an artifact that is absent, truncated or not a JSON object, so a malformed record reads as "nobody looked" rather than as a posture. The INNER values are described but not type-pinned on purpose: this subtree is copied verbatim out of a file under `.panopticon`, which a hostile target can pre-commit, and the posture is disclosure that explicitly does NOT gate (it moves no grade, no gate and no certification). Pinning types here would hand that target a way to make every run exit `artifact invalid` -- a junk posture must be readable AS junk, not a reason to throw the report away. The shape below is what panopticon's own probes write.

host.description: The host the posture was measured on (claude / codex / kimi / generic); null when no readable artifact named one.

schema_version.description: Version of the host-capabilities ARTIFACT's own format -- what a consumer diffing two runs needs before it may compare them at all. Normally an integer; deliberately UNTYPED here, with `probed_at` and the `capabilities` triple, for the reason in this section's description.

probed_at.description: When this posture was last ESTABLISHED (the record is rewritten when something an operator cares about moves, not on every probe), so the interval probed_at..end-of-run is one over which the enforcement posture held unbroken. Normally an ISO-8601 string. Distinct from meta.timestamp, which is synthesis time. Never defaulted: "nobody wrote down when" has to stay distinguishable from a measured moment.

capabilities.description: The artifact's capability map VERBATIM, one entry per capability name (tool_policy_enforced, read_scope_confined, artifact_write_guard, model_binding, usage_ledger), so the REASON survives into the report and two runs can be diffed rather than merely compared. `{}` means nothing was measured, which is a different fact from every capability being refuted.

state.description: `proven`, `refuted` or `unknown`, as written by the probe. `unknown` is NOT benign -- nobody looked -- and is treated exactly as `refuted` wherever posture is consumed; the two are kept apart because they have different remedies. Stated here rather than pinned as an enum, for the reason in this section's description.

by.description: Probe id that established the state (e.g. registered-shell-tools, read-guard-armed, kimi-usage-wire). `null` when no probe ran at all -- an `unknown` row carries its reason in `detail` and nothing in `by`.

detail.description: What the probe actually found, in the probe's own words -- the half of a disclosure that makes it a disclosure rather than a mood. Every agreeing probe's finding, joined.

cli_flags.description: D10 N3: the operational CLI facts ride BESIDE `capabilities`, never inside it, exactly as they do in the artifact -- a consumer diffing two postures must not read a flag that gates nothing as a capability that moved.

integrity.description: Run-integrity reconciliation driving certification: unexpected, duplicate, mislabeled, malformed, content-mismatched, empty, or invalid dispatch artifacts force gate INCONCLUSIVE — as does a fan-out snapshot that is corrupt (content_snapshot_unreadable), owed-but-absent (content_snapshot_missing), or not bound to the bytes this run's driver wrote (content_snapshot_mismatched).

malformed_findings_files.description: #1513: findings files that violate the findings contract, as [{file, cell: [group, domain]|null, defects: [{index, reason}]}]. A stamped cell whose findings list holds a non-object is not a completed clean review; these fail the gate closed and their cells are netted out of the floor audit. Dropped source evidence used to exist only on stderr.

unreadable_name_files.description: #2964: files assigned to a review cell whose prompt spelling is not their name (a control, bidi or surrogate character the prompt escapes), in that inert spelling. Whether a reviewer read them is unknown; sinks certification.

coverage_files_skipped.description: #2080: coverage artifact basenames skipped because they could not be read as objects with usable groups. Any skipped file prevents coverage certification even when the remaining floor audit is empty.

unknown_severity_findings.description: #2990: ids of the findings whose severity was not one of CRITICAL, HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW, INFO (in any case), or (#3210) was absent or null, and was therefore read as CRITICAL, the one reading that fails closed at every --fail-on threshold -- REPORTED, never gating, because the CRITICAL reading already gates. Each such finding keeps its value as written in `severity_as_written`.

sec_less_groups.description: #3245/#3338: groups with code (coverage_model.has_sec_code_surface over their groups.json files, or no file list at all) whose review plan has no SEC cell -- REPORTED, never gating. New runs floor every deterministic code group, so a row here identifies a legacy or malformed coverage artifact; explicit docs/assets-only groups are not named.

cross_domain_findings.description: #calibration-4: findings filed under a domain other than their cell's -- REPORTED, never gating. A reviewer that files a TST finding from an ARC cell has stepped outside its lane, which is a real signal about panel discipline and about catalog gaps (most are `<DOM>-X0X`), but it is evidence about the REVIEW, not about whether the artifacts on disk can be trusted. Treating it as an integrity failure once sank certification on a run whose file integrity was perfect.

ack_stale.description: #493 R2: the on-disk ack did not hash-match any dispatch plan; reported false above when stale.

content_hashes_checked.description: #493 R4: findings files verified against the fan-out snapshot; null = no snapshot (not measured).

content_snapshot_unreadable.description: The fan-out snapshot EXISTS but is corrupt/empty — a tamper signal, not a missing snapshot. Fails the gate closed.

content_snapshot_missing.description: #1511/#1208: the run's dispatch plan declares review cells, so a snapshot was OWED, and none is present — a deleted baseline. Fails the gate closed. False on a run that owes nothing (no driver plan), which keeps the benign 'not measured' reading.

content_snapshot_mismatched.description: #2115: a plan-owed run's present out-file-hashes.json differs from the exact bytes its driver stamped, or has no driver-written digest (including a pre-planted snapshot). Fails the gate closed.

invalid_verify_queue.description: A present verify-queue artifact could not be parsed or had no entries list; forces INCONCLUSIVE.

tools_manifest_invalid.description: #1644/#2070: this run's tools-manifest.json could not be read or cannot bind its exact output receipt to the current run — the reason, else null. With the runner's selected set or receipt untrusted, tool coverage cannot be certified; this sinking integrity fact forces INCONCLUSIVE unless a finding already forces FAIL. An absent manifest stays benign only when no run-bound tool ingest was requested. Other optional malformed fields are repaired at the read (see meta.tools.sanitized / network).

unbound_tool_outputs.description: #2070: scanner-output basenames present in the tools directory but absent from this run's exact output receipt. They are disclosed, never ingested, and force INCONCLUSIVE.

delta_scope_suppressed_git_drivers.description: #2013 fix round 1: the suppressed target Git driver keys that scoped this run's DELTA, else null. Emptying a `filter.*.clean` removes the equality it created between the index blob and the worktree, so git then compares raw worktree bytes against a filtered blob and paths under a suppressed driver compare as MODIFIED (measured: index `ptr payload`, worktree `BIG payload`, plain `git status` clean, the probe's `status` reporting the path modified). On a full-repo scan that costs `target_dirty` in the run manifest and nothing the findings depend on, so `meta.coverage.git_drivers_suppressed` discloses it and certification is unaffected. On a delta-scoped run (`--changes`, or any diff-hunks map with a base: `--scope-changed` / `--pr`) the inflated comparison CHOSE the reviewed file set and the on-diff gate's scope, so this caveat is named, `summary.coverage_certified` is false and `coverage_note` says why. Like every other reason in this section it forces `summary.gate` to INCONCLUSIVE through `integrity_ok`, never past a FAIL. Null means this run was not delta-scoped, or suppressed nothing — never `not measured`.

dispatch_plan_missing.description: SEC-377944137/#1832: the run manifest's own `driver_plan` stamp says this run WROTE a dispatch plan, and no dispatch-plan file is present at synthesis — deleted evidence. Fails the gate closed. #1208's reading of an owed-but-absent fan-out snapshot, applied to the file that decides whether the snapshot is owed at all: deleting the plan silenced the planned-vs-ingested reconciliation, the out_file-collision check, the snapshot obligation and the fan-out accounting at once, so one more `rm` turned a DETECTED findings substitution back into a clean run. The driver no longer re-creates either artifact once it has stamped it, so the absence is reported rather than repaired. False on a run that never wrote a plan (a direct synthesize.py call over hand-collected findings, a target with no declared cells, or a run resumed across the upgrade that added the stamp), which keeps the benign 'not measured' reading every other key here has.

dispatch_plan_mismatched.description: SEC-377944137/#1832: a dispatch plan IS present and parses, but its canonical content does not hash to the `driver_plan` stamp the run manifest recorded when the driver wrote it — substituted evidence. Fails the gate closed. Replacing the plan is the same erasure as deleting it and cheaper: a narrower plan declares fewer cells, so the planned-vs-ingested reconciliation has less to miss and the snapshot obligation shrinks. An UNREADABLE plan is not counted here (the loader reports it as invalid_dispatch_plans; one fault, one key). False when the stamp carries no hash or the run never wrote a plan.

discovery_git_failure.description: #2271: the reason the target's own Git listing FAILED during discovery, so the file surface was found by a raw directory walk instead — a string, else null. A raw walk does not honour the target's `.gitignore`, so this run's reviewed surface may be far larger than the target's own; it is a SUPERSET of the intended one, never a gap in it. Recorded in the run's `groups.json` discovery block and printed on discovery's own stderr, which the driver buffers and discards on a successful run — so this is the only surface it reaches (see also meta.integrity.discovery_files_truncated). It does NOT gate certification: the artifacts on disk are still what they claim to be, which is what this section measures. Null means the Git listing succeeded, the target is not a Git worktree, or no discovery block was present (not measured: a direct synthesize.py call over hand-collected findings, or a run folder written before the block existed); the run's `groups.json` `discovery.method` says which, and is not published in this report (#2271). An empty or non-string reason publishes null too. Free text from git's stderr with a path out of the reviewed tree in it: neutralized and bounded where it is rendered (`synth/integrity.evidence_text`).

discovery_files_truncated.description: #2271: how many discovered files were beyond the discovery cap and therefore never reviewed — the reviewed surface is a PREFIX of the intended one. An integer on every scan, `0` included, because a reader comparing two runs needs to see that this one reviewed the whole tree rather than part of it; on a delta run this counts the changed set, not the repository listing, and `groups.json`'s `discovery.surface` says which; null = not measured (no discovery block: a direct synthesize.py call over hand-collected findings, or a run folder written before the block existed). It does NOT gate certification, which is the precedence this disclosure already had before it reached the report at all. A negative or non-integer count publishes null: it is not a measurement discovery can produce.

cost.description: Dispatch ledger for the run, derived from artifacts (scout profiles, dispatch plans, verify queue). The 4.x cost baseline the 5.x economics work keys on.

tokens.description: Host-reported token usage, read verbatim from <run_dir>/usage.json when the host writes it (#run10 D4). Null when it does not -- never estimated from the dispatch counts.

config.description: #1681 Plan 2 (spec §4): the reviewed repository's own `settings:` section, and what this run did with it. `requested` is what the committed config asked for, verbatim; `effective` is what the trust classes let through (a grain value after its clamp, a gate value at least as strict as panopticon's default); `refused` and `clamped` say what did not survive and why; `disclosures` is the same in prose, as the terminal summary prints it. The maps' KEYS and VALUES come from a target-authored file and are deliberately not type-pinned, for meta.host_capabilities' reason -- this is disclosure that gates nothing, and a junk config must be readable as junk rather than a way to make the report fail its own schema. Empty maps and lists mean the config asked for nothing, which is a measurement, not an absence.

overall_grade.description: Letter banded over summary.health.score: S=100, A>=90, B>=80, C>=70, D>=60, F>=26, X below. S is reachable ONLY at exactly 100 (no gate-eligible weighted defect). Supersedes the max-severity rollup, which saturated -- one HIGH anywhere was a D at any codebase size. null when health is unmeasurable (no readable reviewed LoC) or when coverage is incomplete, in which case provisional_grade carries the letter.

provisional_grade.description: The letter overall_grade would have carried, held back because coverage did not complete. Same bands.

risk_level.description: The worst gate-eligible severity present, LOW when none is. #3220: when no review cell answered, the worst gate-eligible finding is only a lower bound, and null when there is none to bound it.

stats_population.description: Which finding population summary.stats counts. 'active' = non-rejected findings (== findings[]).

gate_severities.description: The gate's reach across the severity distribution. `in_play` = severities at or above --fail-on (any finding there would FAIL); `contributing` = the subset that actually holds a GATE-ELIGIBLE finding, i.e. what the FAIL is made of. Derived from the gate-eligible set, NOT from summary.stats (which counts the ACTIVE set, including unverified findings that cannot gate) -- so `contributing` is non-empty if and only if gate == FAIL. All three fields are empty/null when no --fail-on was given.

fail_on.description: The threshold in force, uppercased; null when no --fail-on was given or it was unrecognised.

in_play.description: Severities at or above the threshold, worst first.

contributing.description: The in-play severities holding at least one gate-eligible finding.

evidence_stats_population.description: Which finding population summary.evidence_stats counts. 'all' = active + discarded (== findings[] + discarded_claims[]).

counts.description: #1059: reconcilable finding-population totals so the two histograms above are never ambiguous. active == len(findings[]); discarded == len(discarded_claims[]); total == active + discarded.

health.description: #1146: secondary size-aware health index reported ALONGSIDE the max-severity letter (never touches the gate or the letter). score = 100 * total_loc / (total_loc + weighted_defect) -- a 0-100 scale where HIGHER is healthier and 100 means no gate-eligible weighted defect; null when both inputs are 0 (nothing reviewed), and (#3220) when no review cell answered. Population is the gate-eligible set, same as the letter. Supersedes total_loc / weighted_defect, which ran backwards, was unbounded above, and returned null for a CLEAN repo; both inputs are still emitted, so any report -- including one written under the old formula -- can be recomputed under either.

score.description: 0-100, higher is healthier. null when total_loc and weighted_defect are both 0, or (#3220) when no review cell answered.

total_loc.description: Non-blank lines across the unique reviewed files (the numerator).

weighted_defect.description: Sum over gate-eligible findings of weight[severity] * lines-spanned, each finding's span capped at `span_cap` lines (#3230).

weights.description: Severity weights used: info 0, low 1, medium 5, high 25, critical 125.

span_cap.description: #3230: the most lines one finding's span counts for in weighted_defect, so citing a whole file cannot outweigh a run's real defects. Absent from a report written before the cap, whose span was unbounded.

formula.description: The exact expression used to compute `score`, so a report is self-describing across formula changes.

delta.description: Delta gate summary: on-diff and pre-existing per-severity counts; null outside delta mode.

panel_grades.description: Per-panel A-F, still the MAX-SEVERITY rollup and deliberately not health-banded: health needs lines of code, and LoC is not attributable per panel (one file feeds several). Do not read these on the same scale as summary.overall_grade.

short_title.description: The title trimmed to issue-title length, derived by findings normalization on EVERY finding (equal to `title` when it already fits). Tool messages are sometimes whole remediation paragraphs; the issue filer, the X0X candidate builder and the strain report all read this and keep the full text in the body.

fingerprint.description: Stable identity of the CLAIM (panel/category/file/title-derived, and, for a tool finding naming an artifact, `tool_evidence.package_name`), the same identity the verify queue keys a verdict on. Exported so a consumer can bind a finding across runs and across the queue. KNOWN DIVERGENCE: the queue disambiguates a collision with a `-<n>` suffix that never appears here, so a fingerprint -> queue_id lookup is ambiguous for a colliding pair.

delta.description: #449 on-diff classification against the run's diff-hunks.json, stamped on every finding in delta mode and absent outside it. `on_diff` fails OPEN (true) where the file changed but the finding carries no line, so a delta gate never silently drops a claim it could not place.

severity_as_written.description: #2990: the finding's severity as written when it was not one of the five known values (in any case); `severity` then reads CRITICAL. Inert text, at most 100 characters before a marked cut. null (#3210): the finding carried no severity (the key absent or null), also read as CRITICAL.

rung.description: OCRDb severity_range rung label (for example raise_when[0]) or its exact condition text.

location.description: #1522: a location, if present, identifies a FILE. line_start is optional -- a whole-file finding (missing header, bad config) is legitimate and must not have a line number invented for it. A finding with no locus at all (a repo-wide catalog- or coverage-gap finding) carries no location key at all; `location` is not in the finding-level required list.

occurrences.description: How many tool findings sharing this panel, category, file, rule id and artifact (`tool_evidence.package_name`) were collapsed into this one, stamped on every tool finding with a rule id by synth/findings.aggregate_tool_findings, or carried onto the surviving finding in `synth/corroborate.dedupe` when that aggregated tool finding is the member DROPPED in favour of a same-category survivor (#2361).

additional_loci.description: The other loci of the tool findings sharing this finding's panel, category, file, rule id and artifact (`tool_evidence.package_name`) that synth/findings.aggregate_tool_findings collapsed into this one (see `occurrences`): the survivor keeps the primary locus in `location` and lists the rest here, lowest line first (a locus with no line first of all), an agent-corroborated locus winning the primary slot -- or carried onto the surviving finding in `synth/corroborate.dedupe` when that aggregated tool finding is the member DROPPED in favour of a same-category survivor (#2361). Absent on a finding that neither aggregated nor absorbed one.

missing_evidence.description: Present with status `backup_scope_limited` (#1638 P16): the files the backup advisor said it was not granted. The primary CONFIRMED stands and the report names what the second opinion could not see, instead of implying it looked and could not tell.

advisor_code.description: The OCRDb code the verify advisor independently landed on, recorded ONLY when it differs from the finding's own `code`. Never applied — the advisor is a second opinion, not an authority on the catalog, so re-coding on one opinion is refused for the same reason severity is untouched. Its presence is the catalog-STRAIN flag: the panel filed one code and an independent re-read preferred another. A value ending `-X0X` means the advisor judged the panel's real code a mis-fit; an `-X0X` finding whose advisor_code is a real code means the reverse. Since #2101 the SYNTHESIS step never applies it either: `synth.codes.apply_verdict_quality` ran later in the live call order and rewrote the finding's `code` from the same value this field records, so each step read correctly on its own and only the composition contradicted this field.

included_by.description: What pulled the vulnerable artifact in, as the tool reported them, written by the dependency-check adapter from its includedBy entries; evidence only, never used as a location; bounded, with a cut list marked by a trailing "N more…" entry.
